summary: The paper adapts crosscoders to track SAE-style features across LLM pre-training snapshots, yielding a clean descriptive account of feature emergence (initialization vs. emergent features, a directional turning point near step 1,000, a complexity-emergence-time correlation) and a causal link to downstream tasks via attribution patching, capped by a hypothesized statistical-to-feature-learning phase transition. The method is clearly presented, the positioning against learning-dynamics theory and sparse dictionary learning is fair, and the limitations are honestly stated. Weaknesses are concentrated in experimental rigor: no seeds/error bars for crosscoder training, a single middle layer per model, a modest LLM-scored complexity correlation (r=0.309, n=100), and a phase-transition claim supported mainly by timing coincidences. Overall this is a sound, useful, borderline-accept contribution consistent with accepted ICLR interpretability papers.
strengths: Genuinely new application: adapting crosscoders to align features across training snapshots is, to my knowledge, novel and enables analyses (per-feature lifetime, directional rotation, dimensionality dynamics) that per-snapshot SAEs cannot directly support.

The decoder-norm-as-feature-strength observation is simple, elegant, and falls out of the sparsity objective; the paper also proactively addresses the two main failure modes (misalignment, feature splitting) with reasoned arguments and appendix evidence.

Connects microscopic feature evolution to macroscopic behavior with complementary ablations (remove-top-k and keep-only-top-k) on SVA, induction, and IOI, showing identified features are approximately necessary and sufficient.
Honest scoping: limitations (Pythia-only, simple tasks, discrete-snapshot cost) are stated plainly, and the phase-transition claim is hedged ('roughly divided').

key_concerns.issue: No variance reporting anywhere: crosscoders appear to be trained once per configuration, with no seeds, error bars, or sensitivity to lambda_sparsity/dictionary size for the qualitative claims (emergence times, lifetimes, turning point at step ~1,000). Feature-level statistics could be unstable across runs.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Train at least 2-3 crosscoders with different seeds/data orderings and report variance for the key statistics (peak-time distribution, lifetime distribution, step-1,000 orthogonality, dimensionality curves).

key_concerns.issue: The statistical-to-superposition phase transition (Section 6) rests on timing coincidence between unigram/bigram KL convergence and feature emergence, plus a dimensionality dip-and-rise; this is correlational and alternative explanations (e.g., LR schedule effects, crosscoder capacity artifacts at early snapshots) are not ruled out.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add controls: show the dimensionality trend is robust to crosscoder size and sparsity level, test whether the turning point shifts under different LR schedules or snapshot subsets, and soften the causal framing of the two-phase claim.

key_concerns.issue: Analysis is restricted to a single middle layer per model (layer 6 of 160M, layer 16 of 6.9B), yet claims are phrased at the level of 'model pre-training' dynamics; feature evolution is known to be layer-dependent.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Repeat at least the Figure 4/5 statistics at one early and one late layer, or explicitly re-scope claims to middle-layer residual-stream features.

key_concerns.issue: The complexity-vs-emergence-time result uses 100 LLM-scored features (Claude Sonnet 4) with a modest correlation (r=0.309); LLM-based complexity scoring is subjective and unvalidated against human judgments in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Validate the rubric against human ratings on a subset, report inter-rater agreement, and increase the sample size.

key_concerns.issue: No baseline for cross-snapshot tracking quality: crosscoders are compared to per-snapshot SAEs only on reconstruction Pareto metrics, not on alignment/tracking fidelity against an alternative (e.g., per-snapshot SAEs with greedy feature matching).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a matching-based SAE baseline and compare consistency of tracked-feature trajectories, or strengthen the linear-probe sanity check (Appendix C) into the main text.

key_concerns.issue: Attribution scores rely on first-order/IG linear approximations whose faithfulness on Pythia-scale models is assumed rather than measured; metric recovery curves are the only validation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report faithfulness of the decomposition (e.g., metric recovery vs. number of features against random-feature controls) for all three tasks.

questions_for_authors: How stable are the headline statistics (peak-emergence distribution, lifetime distribution, the step-1,000 directional turning point) across crosscoder seeds and sparsity coefficients?
Does the step-1,000 turning point coincide with any learning-rate schedule event or optimizer-state effect in Pythia, and how do you rule that out as the cause of the near-orthogonal direction shift?
Why were layer 6 (160M) and layer 16 (6.9B) chosen, and do the qualitative patterns (initialization vs. emergent features, emergence hierarchy) hold at other depths?
For the dimensionality metric in Eq. 6, how sensitive is the dip-and-recovery shape to the crosscoder dictionary size, given that the 6.9B model with 32,768 features shows a much lower final ratio?
Can you quantify how often crosscoder feature splitting (Appendix F) occurs, and does it bias lifetime or emergence-time estimates for highly active features?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well-scoped (the phase transition is framed as 'rough' and limitations are explicit), but the single-layer, single-seed evidence is thinner than the generality implied by the title and Section 6 framing.

significance.justification: Opens a practical methodology for mechanistically studying pre-training dynamics, a topic of high current interest; interpretability and learning-dynamics researchers would plausibly build on and cite it.

novelty.justification: First adaptation of crosscoders to cross-snapshot analysis with several new empirical observations (directional turning point, emergence hierarchy), though the underlying tools (SAEs, crosscoders, attribution patching) are existing.

rigor.justification: Method is sound and failure modes are reasoned through with appendix sanity checks, but the central phase-transition claim is correlational and key proxies (decoder norm as feature strength) rest on appendix-level validation.

statistical_soundness.justification: No seeds, error bars, or run-to-run variance for any crosscoder-derived statistic; the single significance test reported is one modest correlation (r=0.309, p=0.002, n=100) based on LLM-generated scores.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations are candidly stated and the two-phase claim is hedged, though the title and some prose imply broader generality than two Pythia models at one layer support.

clarity.justification: Well-organized, precise notation, and the method and findings are easy to follow; the narrative from features to circuits to phases is coherent.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure with intro, related work, method, experiments, limitations, and conclusion at appropriate length; the abstract content is absent from the extraction, treated as an anonymization artifact.

reproducibility.justification: Models (Pythia), data (SlimPajama), snapshot selection, layer choice, dictionary sizes, thresholds, and task construction are specified, with appendix pointers for hyperparameters; reproduction is feasible assuming the redacted links exist.

related_work.justification: Fair and current coverage of learning-dynamics theory (NTK, IB, SLT) and sparse dictionary learning (SAEs, transcoders, crosscoders), with clear delineation of the contribution.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting displays (Pareto comparisons, norm evolution, lifetime/peak distributions, attribution and ablation curves, KL/dimensionality dynamics) rather than decoration.

breadth_generality.justification: Two models from one family, one layer each, three relatively simple downstream tasks, and no cross-architecture or cross-dataset validation; generality claims are hedged but the empirical base is narrow.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a novel, clearly presented methodology with interesting findings, held back by missing variance reporting, single-layer scope, and a correlational central claim that needs stronger controls.
